title: Emotional Intelligence
shortDescription: Self-awareness, self-regulation, empathy, social awareness and relationship management, based on EQ-i 2.0 and MSCEIT frameworks.
longDescription: Emotional Intelligence measures how you perceive, use, understand, and manage emotions — in yourself and others — across 9 EQ facets drawn from the EQ-i 2.0 and MSCEIT frameworks: Perceiving Emotions, Using Emotions, Understanding Emotions, Managing Emotions, Self-Perception, Self-Expression, Interpersonal Skills, Decision Making, and Stress Management.
sourceNote: Ported verbatim from airostudio/Emotional-Intelligence (public/js/test-questions.js) — 40 real questions across the 9 real EQ facets. A few items reference face images or an original slider mechanic not directly portable as multiple_choice/likert_scale text; those are noted per-question via 'instructions'/'scoringNotes' rather than silently dropped.

sections.name: Perceiving Emotions

sections.instructions: For each item, choose the response that best identifies the emotion shown or described.

resultRanges.title: Developing Emotional Intelligence
resultRanges.description: There are several areas where you can grow your emotional skills. Emotional awareness, expression, and regulation are still forming, which presents great opportunities for personal development.
recommendations: Keep a daily emotion journal to build self-awareness
Practice pausing before reacting when emotions run high
Ask trusted friends or colleagues for feedback on your emotional interactions

resultRanges.title: Average Emotional Intelligence
resultRanges.description: Your emotional intelligence is typical. With focused effort on specific facets, you can significantly enhance how you perceive, use, understand, and manage emotions.
recommendations: Balance emotional and logical considerations when making decisions
Practice active listening and validating others' feelings before problem-solving
Develop healthy coping strategies for stressful situations

resultRanges.title: Strong Emotional Intelligence
resultRanges.description: You have solid emotional skills and generally navigate emotional situations well, with some areas for potential growth.
recommendations: Channel nervous energy into focused attention during high-stakes moments
Continue building resilience through gradual exposure to stress
Practice assertive, 'I'-statement communication in difficult conversations

resultRanges.title: Very Strong Emotional Intelligence
resultRanges.description: You demonstrate strong emotional awareness and management skills, handling both your own emotions and those of others with confidence in most situations.
recommendations: Refine your ability to remain objective when emotions run high
Use positive emotions deliberately to boost creativity and decision quality
Continue strengthening close, mutually satisfying relationships

resultRanges.title: Exceptional Emotional Intelligence
resultRanges.description: You demonstrate outstanding emotional awareness and management skills, excelling at understanding both your own emotions and those of others across nearly all situations.
recommendations: Share your emotional regulation strategies with others as a mentor or coach
Take on high-stakes situations that require sustained composure under pressure
Use your strengths in perceiving and managing emotions to support team dynamics

questions.questionText: Rate the intensity of sadness shown in this expression:
questions.instructions: Originally a 0-100 slider ('Very Mild' to 'Very Intense') compared against a correct intensity of 70. Scoring: 5 pts if |value-70|<20, 3 pts if <40, else 1 pt.

questions.questionText: You need to write a heartfelt condolence letter. Which mood would help you write most effectively?
Which emotional state would best help you brainstorm creative solutions?
You're about to give an important presentation. A moderate level of which emotion would enhance your performance?
When reviewing important financial documents for errors, which emotional state is most helpful?
Which mood helps most when you need to connect deeply with a friend going through a difficult time?
If someone feels disappointed, and the situation continues to get worse, what emotion typically follows?
What emotion results from combining anticipation and joy?
Someone receives unexpected praise for work they didn't think was noticed. What sequence of emotions likely occurs?
Grief is typically a combination of which emotions?
After failing an important exam, which emotional progression is most likely healthy?
A friend shares exciting news while you're feeling down. The best response is to:

options.label: Pretend to be happy and hide your feelings
Tell them you can't deal with their happiness right now
Genuinely share their joy while acknowledging your own feelings privately
Change the subject to your problems

questions.questionText: You receive harsh criticism at work that you feel is unfair. The most effective response is to:

options.label: Suppress all emotions and say nothing
Take time to process, then calmly discuss specific points
Complain to coworkers about the unfairness

questions.questionText: You're angry at a family member. To maintain the relationship, you should:

options.label: Give silent treatment until they apologize
Express your feelings calmly using 'I' statements

questions.questionText: You're feeling anxious before a big event. The best strategy is to:

options.label: Try to completely eliminate the anxiety
Use the nervous energy to enhance your alertness and preparation
Avoid thinking about the event entirely

questions.questionText: A team member is upset about a project setback. To help them, you should:

options.label: Tell them to focus on the positive
Ignore their emotions and focus only on solutions
Validate their feelings first, then collaborate on solutions
Share a time when you had it worse
